sections.purpose: To inspect parenteral preparations (injections, infusions) for the presence of visible particulate matter and clarity as per pharmacopeial requirements (IP, BP, USP).
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmaceutics laboratory for quality control of injectable formulations — mandatory test before batch release.
procedure: Ensure the clarity test apparatus is clean and the black/white background panel and LED light source are functioning correctly.
Switch on the illuminated background and allow the light to stabilize for 5 minutes.
Wipe the exterior of each parenteral container (vial, ampoule, infusion bag) with a lint-free cloth to remove fingerprints.
Hold the container by the neck or base — do not touch the body of the container.
Gently swirl the container to resuspend any settled particles — do not introduce air bubbles.
Inspect against the white background for dark particles (glass fragments, rubber particles, precipitates).
Inspect against the black background for light-coloured or translucent particles.
Examine each container for a minimum of 5 seconds against each background.
Classify each unit: Pass — clear solution, free from visible particles; Reject — any visible particle, cloudiness, discolouration, or leakage.
For ampoule inspection: check for correct fill volume (compare against reference ampoule) and seal integrity.
Record the number of units inspected, number rejected, and reason for rejection.
After inspection, clean the viewing area with a damp cloth and cover the lamp when not in use.
Document results as per batch record requirements.
precautions: Perform the test in a draught-free area with a controlled background — stray light affects visibility.
Illumination intensity must comply with pharmacopeial requirements: 2000–3750 lux for small volume parenterals (IP/USP).
The inspector's visual acuity must be corrected to 6/6 (with or without corrective lenses).
Do not inspect with bare hands that may contaminate the outer surface of containers.
Do not introduce vigorous agitation — this may dissolve fine particulates or generate air bubbles that mimic particles.
Inspect under both black and white backgrounds as different particles are visible against different backgrounds.
Calibrate the light source intensity periodically using a calibrated lux meter.
Train and qualify all personnel performing clarity inspection — inter-operator variability must be controlled.
